clause_inventory.quote: Aurora Software Private Limited (P01, Customer) and Forge Electronics Private Limited (P02, Provider) agree to hosting service SVC-ATLAS for Aurora application APP-ATLAS. The same parties also contract in different capacities under C02; this hosting agreement retains its own obligations and remedies. Company legal notice address: aurora-legal@aurora.example. Counterparty legal notice address: legal@forge.example.

This agreement is signed on 2026-12-15 and runs from 2026-12-15 through 2027-12-14 inclusive. It expires without automatic renewal. The fixed hosting fee is INR 200,000 per calendar month, due on the fifth day of that month at 17:00 UTC. No late-payment charge is agreed. The initial 2026-12-15 through 2026-12-31 period is charged at the full monthly fee and is first due on 2026-12-20 at 17:00 UTC; the regular fifth-day rule applies thereafter.

For each distinct incident of more than 60 consecutive minutes of complete unavailability of SVC-ATLAS, Provider owes Customer a credit of INR 10,000. An incident of exactly 60 minutes does not qualify. Distinct incidents must have separate restoration and outage records. Total credits are capped at INR 20,000 per UTC calendar month of outage start. Credits are recoverable by Customer and are not Customer liabilities.

An incident is excluded from clause 3.1 of C01 only if Customer approved that specific maintenance window at least 48 hours before its start and the outage was wholly inside that window. Provider scheduling alone is not approval. If approval evidence is missing, applicability is unresolved pending evidence; do not presume approval or its absence.

Customer must email a claim identifying the incident within 10 calendar days after restoration to claims@forge.example. A valid claim is due by 17:00 UTC on the tenth following calendar date. Credits are the sole monetary remedy for service unavailability under this agreement; no downstream damages are reimbursed.

Provider restoration logs identify incident ID, service ID, start, end and any scheduled window. A later signed approval record may supply earlier approval evidence. A repeated log for the same incident is not a second outage. Corrected records supersede the identified prior record without creating another incident.

For a material breach other than service unavailability, written notice must be received at legal@forge.example. Provider has 10 calendar days after receipt to cure, ending at 17:00 UTC on the tenth following date. Customer may serve a separate termination notice only after that deadline if the breach remains uncured.

Indian law governs this agreement. Courts in Bengaluru have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes under this agreement. This provision neither chooses the forum for other contracts nor promises consolidated proceedings.

All times are UTC and all days are calendar days. There is no weekend or holiday adjustment. A deadline stated as a date ends at 17:00 UTC unless another time is explicit. Financial amounts exclude taxes, which are outside this agreement. No terms from an absent document may be assumed.
Mira Sen for Aurora and Anil Das for Forge record execution on 2026-12-15.

The monthly service-credit cap in clause 3.1 is INR 20,000. For other claims, each party aggregate liability is capped at INR 1,000,000, except fraud, wilful misconduct and indemnity obligations. Downstream service liabilities are not reimbursed under this agreement.

A party whose supplied hosting materials infringe third-party intellectual property, or whose unauthorized disclosure produces a third-party claim, shall indemnify the other for that claim and reasonable defense costs. The protected party must give prompt notice and cooperate in the defense.

Hosting configurations, access keys and the other party commercial information shall be disclosed only to personnel who need them for this hosting service and owe confidentiality duties. Use for another purpose is prohibited. Protection continues for 3 years after termination, except for information public without breach.

Each party must comply with laws applicable to its role in hosting facilities. This includes the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable and GDPR where its processing scope applies. Personal-data processing requires access controls and a documented incident-response procedure. No ISO certification is promised.

Transfer of the hosting agreement needs the other party written consent. An affiliate transfer is permitted on 30 calendar days written notice only if the original party remains liable. A change of control does not substitute a new party or waive required consent.

Relief for an event beyond reasonable control is confined to the affected obligations in hosting facilities. The affected party must give written notice within 5 calendar days after discovery, explain causation and provide mitigation evidence. Accrued payments remain payable. Neither an outage nor supplier delay qualifies automatically.

The parties remain free to enter other arrangements outside the scope of hosting facilities. This agreement grants no exclusivity or non-compete except any restriction expressly stated in this clause.

Either party may end future hosting facilities for convenience by written notice received at the other party legal notice address at least 30 calendar days before termination. Accrued payment obligations, express survival provisions and the stated conditions of any early-exit fee continue to apply.
